title: Gaussian gradient bound from rotational variation
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ at $x$, and suppose that $x\mapsto L(x)$ is continuous. Let $C\in[0,\infty]$. If for every real $\theta>0$ the Gaussian integral of $\sqrt{\pi/2}\,|f(\cos\theta\,z_1+\sin\theta\,z_2)-f(z_1)|/\theta$ over independent standard Gaussian vectors $z_1,z_2\in\mathbb R^n$ is at most $C$, then $\int \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (L(x)e_i)^2}\,d\gamma_n(x)\le C$, as a nonnegative extended integral.
hypotheses_covered: $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ has derivative $L(x)$ at every $x$
The derivative map $x\mapsto L(x)$ is continuous
For every $\theta>0$, the extended Gaussian integral of the normalized rotational variation is at most $C$
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x)$, and put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. Assume $L$ is continuous and $C\in[0,\infty]$. If $\mathbb E(\sqrt{\pi/2}\,|f(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)-f(X)|/\theta)\le C$ for every $\theta>0$, then $\mathbb E|L(X)|_2\le C$, with all expectations nonnegative extended integrals.
